content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Little Rock

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of education and project-management experience. Review PMI's current eligibility criteria—typically a bachelor's degree plus years of documented project leadership, or an associate degree with additional experience. Gather your project documentation and work history before applying.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp. Our instructor-led course covers the PMBOK® Guide framework, exam domains, and real-world application. Attend sessions on your schedule from anywhere, interact with active certified practitioners, and receive study materials designed to prepare you for exam day.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Create your PMI account and submit your formal PMP application, including your education credentials and documented project experience. Pay the associated PMI exam fee. PMI will review and approve your application, granting you eligibility to schedule your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-prep resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor office hours—to solidify your knowledge. Schedule your computer-based exam through Pearson VUE. Sit for the PMP exam and demonstrate your mastery of project-management practices and leadership.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) over a standard three-year renewal cycle to keep your credential active. Pursue continuing education, serve in your professional community, or lead projects. Renew with PMI before expiration to maintain the PMP mark.
